props.title: What does a Spanish guitarist play?
props.lede: The song list usually includes classic Spanish guitar pieces like Malagueña and Entre dos Aguas, along with rumbas and tangos. Many guests won’t know the names, but almost everyone recognizes the sound. We can also play familiar songs in the same style. Can’t Help Falling in Love is a popular choice for a processional, for instance, and the Beatles sound great on Spanish guitar.

props.html: It’s all instrumental. At a wedding, the guitarist will follow what’s happening, so the music can keep going while guests find their seats and wrap up when the wedding party reaches the front. We’ll put the song list together with you, and if you want a song that isn’t on it, let us know when you book and we can usually learn it.
Prefer blues, roots or jazz? Check out our solo guitarist. Want some more ideas? Take a look at our full song list.

rows.text: A Spanish guitarist can play the whole ceremony, from the prelude and processional to the recessional, and any quiet moment in between. It’s an excellent choice if you want something warm and romantic.
Rumbas and familiar songs make a great cocktail hour, at a volume where your guests can talk easily.

rows.term: The dinner party, and the milestone birthday
rows.text: A Spanish guitarist can play through the whole meal, and it’s an easy way to make a dinner or birthday feel like a special occasion, whether you’re in Denver or up in the mountains.
A solo guitarist is a nice touch for a client dinner or member event, and it makes the evening feel thoughtfully planned.
Looking for just an hour of music? We can do that for a proposal, a toast at a 60th Birthday or an anniversary surprise.
We can play a memorial or graveside service, with the music your family chooses.

props.html: Want to know more? We’ve answered more common questions here.

items.q: Is Spanish guitar the same as flamenco?
items.a: Not exactly. Flamenco is one style of Spanish guitar music, and our guitarists mix it with other Spanish pieces and familiar songs.

About as loud as a conversation at the next table. Indoors, the guitar usually doesn't need a sound system at all. Outdoors, or if your officiant needs a microphone, we can bring a small sound system and set it to the right level for your venue.
One of the Spanish guitarists on our roster, and we'll let you know who it is when you book.

items.q: Can a Spanish guitarist play a wedding ceremony outdoors?
items.a: Yes. We'll just need a covered, level, dry spot, plus power if you're using a sound system, and we'll work out a backup plan with you in case of weather.
